chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Sayyabah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man asked him, saying: 'I am your ransom; I hear people saying that farming is disliked.' He said: 'Farm and plant, by Allah, people have not done any deed more permissible and more pure than it. And by Allah, we will certainly farm the crops and plant the palms after the emergence of the Dajjal.'
ai.seo_question: Is farming considered disliked or recommended in Shia Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) vigorously refutes the notion that farming is disliked (makruh), elevating it to a highly virtuous and pure deed that pleases God. He underscores the enduring significance of agriculture by predicting that he and the Imams will personally engage in sowing and planting even after the emergence of the Dajjal, highlighting its eschatological and practical value in Shia tradition.
